mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant above 5% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to persistent risk aversion from higher real rates compressing equity discounting.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative in at least 70% of similar high-rate regimes, or FEDFUNDS never exceeds 5% in the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected monthly increase in employment (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which is associated with positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month AND UNRATE < previous month
failure_condition: Over 60-day window, returns are not statistically different from baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or labor momentum reverses before the 60-day horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in consumer demand proxies (HOUST) coinciding with a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a shift from supply-side to demand-side constraints, predicting positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by > 10% month-over-month AND INDPRO decreases by > 5% month-over-month
failure_condition: No significant return advantage in 20-day horizon, or divergence reverses before the window closes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) for three consecutive months is interpreted as a supply shock, leading to negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically negative in > 80% of such supply contraction episodes.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 3% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to market anticipation of tighter policy.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive in > 50% of such episodes, or inflation decays before the 20-day window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in payrolls (PAYEMS) without a corresponding rise in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a robust labor market, predicting positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns in normal regimes.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases for three consecutive months AND UNRATE remains below 4.0% over the same period
failure_condition: No significant return advantage in 60-day horizon, or unemployment rises above 4.0% during the period.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden one-time spike in retail sales demand proxies (HOUST) followed by a return to trend is associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to temporary optimism.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by > 15% month-over-month and reverts to previous month's trend within 2 weeks
failure_condition: No significant return advantage in 20-day window, or the spike is not confirmed by subsequent data.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) remains flat for four consecutive months, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is predicted to be negative due to persistent supply-side stagnation.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO is flat for four consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically negative in > 60% of such episodes.
